Our delivery methodology for PITB is a controlled, multi-site rollout that ensures standardisation across all six regional offices while protecting service continuity. We will execute under our ISO 9001 quality management system and ISO 27001 information security management system [CO-PROFILE], with governance led by PMP-certified project managers [CO-PROFILE].

We will start with a joint discovery and design validation phase to confirm current-state inventories, room readiness, fibre/copper pathways, IP/VLAN plan, routing, security zoning, and acceptance criteria. This is followed by a detailed Low Level Design and implementation plan that enforces redundancy at the core (dual devices, dual uplinks, diverse paths where feasible) and a documented high-availability cutover sequence to avoid single points of failure.

Implementation will be delivered in repeatable site “waves”:
1) Pre-staging and baseline configuration in our lab (standard templates for switches/routers/firewalls, secure admin, backups). 
2) Structured cabling and fibre backbone installation, testing, and as-built documentation. 
3) On-site installation, configuration, and commissioning with controlled migration windows and rollback procedures. 
4) Centralised monitoring/management onboarding with alerting and reporting; our library evidences network design deployments at scale, but does not yet evidence a specific named monitoring platform—this will be addressed via OEM toolsets and agreed PITB NOC requirements during design finalisation. 

We evidence delivery of enterprise network/data-centre scale design and deployment engagements valued above PKR 30M, including PKR 44M, PKR 182M and PKR 133M projects completed within the last five years [CAP-021][CAP-009][CAP-033].

For warranty and support, we will align the operating model to PITB’s 24x7 helpdesk expectation; our evidenced support model is an in-country desk with 24–48 hour response SLAs [CO-PROFILE], and we will close the four-hour on-site critical response requirement through a PITB-approved escalation and regional field-engineer roster.

Mandatory single-OEM/authorisation: our library does not yet evidence holding a specific OEM partner/reseller authorisation; we will address this by proposing a single OEM stack and submitting the required authorisation letter from the selected OEM prior to award/ordering.

We will complete structured knowledge transfer for PITB operations (runbooks, as-builts, configuration backups, and hands-on training) as part of commissioning [CO-PROFILE].
